title: Third-derivative invariance bound
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a multilinear coefficient family on $n$ coordinates of degree at most $k$. Suppose the $2n$ real random variables $Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}$ are mutually independent, each is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive for some $0<\rho<1$, and each has mean $0$ and second moment $1$. If $\psi\in C^3(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi'''|$ everywhere, then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_L))-\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_R))\right|\le \frac C3\left(\frac1\rho\right)^{3k}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^{{3}/{2}},
\]
where $F(Z)(\omega)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(\omega)$ and $\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]$ is the influence of the Walsh-basis function defined by the same coefficients.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a multilinear coefficient family of degree at most $k$
The $2n$ random variables indexed by the two coordinate copies are mutually independent
Every random variable has mean zero
Every random variable has second moment one
The absolute value of the third derivative of $\psi$ is bounded everywhere by $C$
